newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 31.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- South Korea's Agency for National Security Planning arrested a Korean resident in Japan for spying, the first arrest resulting from information by Hwang Jang-yop, the highest ranking defector from Pyongyang.
- Ruling and opposition lawmakers agreed on Wednesday to form a 18-member committee to devise meaures for political reform. The committee will start work on August 5.
- Kia Group creditors demanded that executives of the country's eighth largest conglomerate give up their managerial rights to receive emergency loans.
- Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi will come to Seoul on Sunday for a three-day offical visit to discuss ways to enhance bilateral political and economic ties.
